BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
- Employee bonuses: DD-005 AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- Ironquay IP: broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- Export/privacy incident (DD-006): preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.
- Title: require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- Tax/IP terms remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Basis:** Our Buyer Negotiation Playbook. The Seller's documents are treated as counterparty material.

## Preliminary point: the "[STANDARD]" labels and the "Reviewer Efficiency Note"

The Seller has marked most clauses "[STANDARD]". Its note says these "have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny" and that we "have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package."

**We should reject this.** Nothing in our playbook or the record shows Wattlebridge has agreed any of these positions. Several "[STANDARD]" positions contradict our playbook outright, and some contradict the Seller's own Disclosure Letter.

- The labels are a one-sided assertion, not an agreed status.
- I have reviewed every clause in full.
- The response to the Seller should state that no term is agreed until both sides sign.

---

## Issue-by-issue review

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** Cap of 20% of the price (AUD 4,800,000), marked [STANDARD].
- **Buyer should want:** 25% of the price (AUD 6,000,000).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.**
- **Reason:** 20% is a fallback that needs Amelia Frost's prior written authority for this draft, and she has not given it.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** De minimis of AUD 25,000. Basket of AUD 250,000. Only the excess over the basket is recoverable.
- **Buyer should want:** De minimis of AUD 5,000. Basket of AUD 50,000. Once the basket is exceeded, the Seller is liable from the first dollar.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Counter at AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000, first-dollar recovery.**
- **Reason:** The Seller's thresholds are five times ours, and an "excess-only" basket permanently writes off AUD 250,000 of valid loss.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months after Completion. It also proposes that every limitation applies to all Claims "unless expressly stated otherwise".
- **Buyer should want:** 24 months after Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Counter at 24 months.** Also reject the "applies to all Claims" default (see SPA-N-014).
- **Reason:** 18 months is a fallback that needs Amelia Frost's written approval, and none has been given.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental and Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties would carry the same caps and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer should want:** A separate regime with:
  - a 100% cap;
  - a claims period of at least six years;
  - no application of the general basket, de minimis or knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.**
- **Reason:** Title is the core of what we are buying. Capping it at 20% would leave 80% of the price unprotected if the Seller does not own what it is selling.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** No carve-out. Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply the limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature". On its face, that covers fraud.
- **Buyer should want:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all of the following, to the maximum extent enforceable:
  - caps;
  - baskets;
  - time limits;
  - exclusive remedy;
  - non-reliance.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Insert an express carve-out.** This is non-negotiable and no one may waive it.
- **Reason:** As drafted, a Seller who commits fraud would still benefit from the cap, the time bar and the non-reliance clause.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** Disclosure Letter clauses 1.1 and 1.2 deem disclosed everything in the data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, the statutory registers and public records.
- **Buyer should want:** Only specific, fair disclosure against particular warranties.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Delete general disclosures 1.1 and 1.2.**
- **Reason:** Whole-data-room and public-register disclosure would quietly qualify every warranty.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** Clause 8.3 bars any claim on a matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer should want:** The blanket exclusion deleted. If any qualifier survives, it must:
  - rely on named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry;
  - never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Delete clause 8.3.**
- **Reason:** Clause 8.3 works with SPA-N-006 to wipe out warranty protection, and would even defeat the indemnities for matters we found in due diligence.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Says the consent is "addressed". It offers reasonable endeavours only, with the condition treated as satisfied once Bluefen delivers a written consent.
- **The Seller's own documents conflict:** Disclosure Letter clause 2 confirms that no final consent exists and there is no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied. Bluefen is about AUD 3,600,000, or roughly 30% of FY26 revenue.
- **Buyer should want:** An effective consent, plus evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied, both as a Condition Precedent to Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.**
- **Reason:** Delivery of a consent letter is not an effective consent, and reasonable endeavours alone is not enough for a customer worth 30% of revenue.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** A release of the roughly AUD 3,200,000 facility, provided after Completion.
- **The Seller's own documents conflict:** Disclosure Letter clause 3 confirms the facility has not been repaid and no discharge is available. The change-control provision (8.1) and discharge provision (9.2) are live.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - a current payout letter;
  - direct repayment to Riverlark from Completion funds;
  - executed security releases delivered at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject a post-Completion release.**
- **Reason:** We would be paying the full price while the Company's assets are still encumbered. A post-Completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval, and we have neither.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** The funds flow "reflects agreed mechanics". The bonuses are described as "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised.
- **What the disclosure shows:** Disclosure Letter clause 5 confirms the AUD 420,000 is not in the funds flow. The on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation and similar) are not addressed.
- **Buyer should want:** The AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs as either a specific funds-flow line item or a Seller-funded deduction, backed by an indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the current funds flow.**
- **Reason:** These bonuses only become payable on Completion, so the Company, and therefore we, would bear the cost unless it is expressly allocated to the Seller.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "considered adequate".
- **Buyer should want:** A broader indemnity covering:
  - IP ownership and transfer of the Project Materials;
  - third-party claims;
  - any Ironquay claim.
  The SOW3 cure must be preserved, meaning payment followed by a confirmatory assignment.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject as too narrow.** Note that the AUD 180,000 recorded in DD-010 is not independently verified in either direction (Disclosure Letter clause 4).
- **Reason:** Under DD-004 clause 7.3, IP transfer depends on payment of every SOW3 fee. There is no receipt and no assignment, so the risk to IP ownership goes beyond one invoice.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material".
- **Facts as disclosed:** A download link was sent to an unintended external address. Up to about 1,240 records may be involved. Access, scope and any notification duty are all unknown.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - a covenant to preserve logs;
  - a completed investigation;
  - regular updates before Completion;
  - an appropriate warranty or indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept the "not material" characterisation, and do not overstate the incident either.** We should not assert a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or any monetary figure.
- **Reason:** The facts are not established, so we need contractual protection that responds to whatever the investigation finds.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** The three renewals (AUD 330,000 in total) are "ordinary-course operating costs".
- **What the disclosure shows:** Disclosure Letter clause 8 does not say whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.
- **Buyer should want:** A proper assessment of DD-008 and DD-011 read together, covering timing, scope and whether the renewals are related.
- **Recommendation:** **Neither accept nor reject yet. Raise information requests.**
- **Reason:** The playbook calls for assessment without automatically treating the renewals as Debt or deducting them from the price, and the Seller's label is unsupported.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Two provisions blur the categories:
  - clause 12.3/13 says limitations apply to "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise";
  - clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 say the limitations apply to "all Claims of any nature".
- **Buyer should want:** Title, Tax, IP, payment/indemnity and covenant claims kept as separate categories, with no default that pulls them into the general regime.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Reverse the default so that the general limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims.
- **Reason:** These drafting defaults are a hidden override that would subject every specific protection to the 20% cap and 18-month bar.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012".
- **What the disclosure shows:** Disclosure Letter clause 10 itself concedes that this only identifies the source relied on and that the Buyer has not verified title.
- **Buyer should want:** Independent evidence of:
  - title and ownership;
  - the absence of encumbrances (for example, PPSR and ASIC searches);
  - Seller authority and capacity;
  - executed transfers and share certificates at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the register as sufficient proof.**
- **Reason:** DD-012 is an internal record supplied by the Seller, not independent proof of title.

### SPA-N-016: Tax and IP open terms
- **Seller:** Considers the tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer should want:** These terms remain OPEN. Our position assumes no unlimited liability and that nothing has been resolved.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "settled" characterisation. Keep both terms open for negotiation.**
- **Reason:** No agreement has been reached. Folding Tax and IP into the general regime prejudges an open point and contradicts SPA-N-014.

---

## Summary

| Status | Issues |
|---|---|
| **Reject: playbook baseline** | 001, 002, 003, 004, 006, 007, 014 |
| **Reject: non-negotiable** | 005 (fraud carve-out) |
| **Reject: Seller's own disclosure contradicts its position** | 008, 009, 010, 015 |
| **Reject and broaden** | 011 |
| **Hold the line: unresolved facts** | 012, 013, 016 |

**Escalation:** None of the playbook fallbacks are available. These are the 20% cap and 18-month claims period (SPA-N-001 and SPA-N-003) and the post-Completion Riverlark release (SPA-N-009). Each needs Amelia Frost's written authority, and she has not given it. If the team wants to use any of them, that authority must be obtained first, identifying this draft.

**Suggested covering note to Seller's counsel:** We do not accept that any clause has been "cleared" or that any framework has been agreed. The [STANDARD] designations are rejected and our mark-up covers the full package.

- **Buyer should want:** A proper assessment of DD-008 and DD-011 read together, covering timing, scope and whether the renewals are related.
- **Recommendation:** **Neither accept nor reject yet. Raise information requests.**
- **Reason:** The playbook calls for assessment without automatically treating the renewals as Debt or deducting them from the price, and the Seller's label is unsupported.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Two provisions blur the categories:
  - clause 12.3/13 says limitations apply to "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise";
  - clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 say the limitations apply to "all Claims of any nature".
- **Buyer should want:** Title, Tax, IP, payment/indemnity and covenant claims kept as separate categories, with no default that pulls them into the general regime.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Reverse the default so that the general limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims.
- **Reason:** These drafting defaults are a hidden override that would subject every specific protection to the 20% cap and 18-month bar.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012".
- **What the disclosure shows:** Disclosure Letter clause 10 itself concedes that this only identifies the source relied on and that the Buyer has not verified title.
- **Buyer should want:** Independent evidence of:
  - title and ownership;
  - the absence of encumbrances (for example, PPSR and ASIC searches);
  - Seller authority and capacity;
  - executed transfers and share certificates at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the register as sufficient proof.**
- **Reason:** DD-012 is an internal record supplied by the Seller, not independent proof of title.

### SPA-N-016: Tax and IP open terms
- **Seller:** Considers the tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer should want:** These terms remain OPEN. Our position assumes no unlimited liability and that nothing has been resolved.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "settled" characterisation. Keep both terms open for negotiation.**
- **Reason:** No agreement has been reached. Folding Tax and IP into the general regime prejudges an open point and contradicts SPA-N-014.
